discovery: Development of high-resolution angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) into a momentum-resolved probe of electronic structure and many-body interactions in quantum materials

nominees.name: Zhi-Xun Shen
nominees.affiliation: Stanford University and SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics (experimental spectroscopy of quantum materials)
motivation: The nominees turned angle-resolved photoemission from a band-mapping tool into a precise, momentum-resolved measurement of the single-particle spectral function in strongly correlated matter. Shen's group made the first direct observation of the anisotropic d-wave superconducting gap in the cuprates and later discovered the pseudogap's momentum structure. Campuzano and collaborators showed that the pseudogap has Fermi arcs and measured the sharpening of the Bogoliubov quasiparticle below Tc. Johnson and others found the bosonic 'kinks' in quasiparticle dispersions that reveal electron coupling to collective modes. Together these advances made ARPES the standard probe for cuprates, iron pnictides, topological insulators and moire materials. It settled long-standing questions about gap symmetry and gave a direct view of many-body renormalization. This is a new way of seeing electrons in solids, now used at every synchrotron and in many laboratories worldwide.
